reviews.review: Never has a 40k game felt more right. This is exactly how it should be done. Non-stop, balls to the wall action and carnage from beginning to end. Excellent.

Might be my top game of 2011. 
Crunching melee combat stops this from being another run of the mill Gears of War clone and lifts it into its own class. 
The PvP mulitplayer mode was also a blast though limited in map selection.
SPACE MARINE!??! One of my all time favorite games. Slicing down ork after ork is fantastic. Everything has a satisfying weight to it. 10/10 all the way.

Really awesome 3rd person shoot/beat em up! I've sen alot of crying about character development, or the lack there of when it comes to creating characters you empathize with. ♥♥♥♥ that. This game is a visceral gorefest full of tons of baddies, and an arsenal of intriguing weapons, and really kick ass execution moves. There is no cover system, but I think that would just make it feel like a Gears rip-off instead of a very dynamic, fast paced, blood soaked romp that never really got the credit it deserved. See this guy on Steam sale, pick it up!

Definitely an action game that any Warhammer 40,000 fan should have. You play as a Space Marine captain.
The combat is glorious...being able to hack and slash hordes of enemies as a space marine is a very enjoyable and satisfying experience. However, you need to balance this with use of various ranged weapons, which are also fun to use. My only complaint is that to regenerate health in the single player campaign, you need to perform a brutal finishing move on an enemy, but this move takes time and you can take damage as you perform it. You could argue that it makes gameplay more challenging.
As you continue through the single player campaign, you'll gain access to more weapons, but you can only carry a maximum of three at any given time, so you'll need to choose which weapon is appropriate for the level you're playing.
Storyline is not amazing, but good enough to maintain interest. One could argue that there aren't enough varied environments as you progress through the single player campaign, but this never bothered me.
There are several online modes available. You have two characters, a Space Marine and a Chaos Marine for online play. They are both identical except for appearance. You can fully customise their appearances, weapons and perks in a similar system to the Call of Duty games, with more unlocking as you level up through online play.
Online multiplayer is fun, but the community is full of experienced high level players, which can turn some players off pvp. As for multiplayer pve, there are only two series of maps available, which isn't enough variety to maintain interest for long.
There are DLC options, most of which are cosmetic, available. There are two gameplay DLCs, which enhance the online multiplayer aspect, but I have been told that people rarely use them anymore, so joining a match using the gameplay DLC may be tricky unless you have friends who you know play them regularly. 
Overall it is an action game worth having a look at.
